handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 46 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. Independent second reading is required before integration as reviewed.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: First-pass evidence notes
div.note: The large N extends beside the first couplet. Two short lines of marginal capitals are present to the right: SOMNI is a tentative reading of the first, while the second is too faint to transcribe confidently. No completed title has been supplied. The et ligature is represented schematically and expanded in TEI.
The middle word is tentatively uitabam; faded or disturbed ink prevents a fully secure reading. No erased prior state is asserted.
The last two words are faint and tentatively read aestus erat.
The centre-right words candida uacca are affected by faded ink and local discoloration; retained as unclear.
The first phrase is very faint; Taurus erat comes is tentative. The rest is more legible. No substitute phrase has been introduced from another witness.
The first three words are faint; Cumque sua tenerum is tentative.
Staining at the left obscures the beginning. Dum iacet is tentative; the et sign and the later words remain distinguishable. This is not identified as scribal cancellation.
Staining extends through the first phrase, tentatively Atque iterum pasto. The later pascitur ante cibo is more secure.

The beginning of this physical verse is too faint and stained to reconstruct securely. Only tentative adimente ferendi is retained from its right-hand traces. The gap describes unreadable source text, not a manuscript omission.
At the bottom of image 88 the verse beginning is unreadable in this photograph. Tentative deposuisse and clear caput remain; no familiar complete verse was used to fill the gap.
Image 89 left begins this verse. Its final auras is faint; the following poem begins beneath position 46 on the same physical page, so all 46 assigned positions belong to the extant written sequence.
Venit at the beginning is extremely faint. The et sign and later words are legible.
The opening appears to read Carpitur; its letters and the following pabulo laeta are tentative. The ending is too faint to complete. The apparent unusual reading is preserved rather than normalized.
The opening is faded beyond a secure reading. The sequence gregibus, tentative se immiscuit, and final illis remains visible.

A large dark stain and bright central hole or surface loss obscure the middle of the line. Tentative herbae felicior survives to its left; unreadable spans remain gaps. The physical feature is not treated as deliberate deletion, and its cause is not assigned.

Faint traces across the whole verse do not support a complete reading. Only tentative excussere is retained. An independent reader should re-examine the full line; no human decision is assigned by this working note.
Fading and a large dark patch at the left prevent a continuous reading. Tentative uidisse is retained amid explicit gaps.
The left portion is stained, and the remaining letters are faint. Only tentative fidem is retained; no complete sentence is reconstructed.
The left portion is obscured and most remaining letters are faint. Tentative singula is retained amid gaps.
The visible central sequence is tentatively tale est simulacrum. Both sides remain unreadable; this is a partial first-pass decipherment, not a supplied full reading.
Heavy staining and fading prevent a continuous reading. Tentative consule is the only retained word.
Dark patches obscure the left part of the verse. Tentative est and the final puella can be distinguished; intervening and preceding spans remain gaps.

The physical line was inspected at full resolution and enlarged. Its traces do not yet support a defensible continuous reading or secure complete word in this pass; a one-verse illegibility gap preserves the extant position.
Heavy dark staining obscures much of the verse and the surviving right-side ink is faint. The line is represented conservatively as illegible, not as absent.
Only tentative amore is retained from the faint right-side text. A darker angled mark nearby has no safely established function or letter reading and is not used to infer a correction.
Most left-side ink is obscured by a dark patch; the faint right-side traces do not support secure words in this pass. The extant line remains represented by a gap.
The line is visible but too stained and faint for defensible words in this first pass. A gap is retained without inferring source absence.
A large initial L is tentatively distinguishable at the left edge of the stain. The rest remains unreadable. The initial is not enough evidence to reconstruct the verse.
Only tentative diu is retained from the middle of this faded line; surrounding spans are gaps.
Dixerat is clear at the left. The subsequent interpres gelido mihi is tentative, and the right end disappears into a large dark patch. No complete verse is reconstructed.
The final verse is obscured by fading and the lower-right dark patch. Tentative oculos survives; the remaining words are gaps. The next poem has its own initial on the following physical line.
